run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Root cause: the `frontend` Service in namespace `hotel-reservation` (kind Service, name frontend) selects pods by label `service-route: frontend`, and that label was placed on the `search` Deployment as well as the `frontend` Deployment. As a result the `frontend` Service's Endpoints object contains two addresses on port 5000: frontend pod frontend-5566ddfbfb-f9vj8 (10.244.7.217) and search pod search-9cd459687-5ghvg (10.244.125.41), but the search container exposes only ports 8082 (gRPC) and 9092 (metrics), so any connection to the Service that kube-proxy sends to the search pod cannot be served. The Service probe `frontend.hotel-reservation:5000` failed at 01:18:04 with a 5.0004 s duration (previously a 4.6 ms failure at 01:17:04), while `search.hotel-reservation:8082` probed successfully at the same instant. The frontend and search pods themselves are healthy (HTTP 200 spans, sub-2 ms gRPC spans, zero restarts, no error log lines after startup). Change evidence: the frontend Deployment and search Deployment were both rewritten (generation 2) by manager `OpenAPI-Generator` at 01:17:45 and 01:17:46, creating ReplicaSets frontend-5566ddfbfb and search-9cd459687 whose templates carry label `service-route: frontend`; the pre-existing ReplicaSets frontend-68745cb99c and search-567bb6c4b8 carried only `io.kompose.service`, and the `frontend` Service was patched by manager `kubectl-patch` at 01:17:47. The earlier burst of search→rate `Unavailable/Canceled` warnings at 01:17:46 is a cold-start artifact (rate finished registering in Consul at 01:17:46.6 and its limiter counters show 49 received / 49 completed / 0 rejected / 0 expired), not this fault. Metrics and traces only exist from 01:17:04/01:17:46 to the window end, so no pre-change baseline exists and the exact fraction of client requests lost to the bad endpoint is unverified.

claims.text: The `frontend` Service in namespace hotel-reservation has selector `{"service-route":"frontend"}`; it is the only Service in the whole cluster whose selector uses the `service-route` label, and it was created 2026-11-24T01:17:31Z and later patched by manager `kubectl-patch` at 2026-11-24T01:17:47Z.
The `frontend` Service's Endpoints object lists two addresses on port 5000: search pod search-9cd459687-5ghvg at 10.244.125.41 and frontend pod frontend-5566ddfbfb-f9vj8 at 10.244.7.217.

The `search` Deployment's pod template labels are `io.kompose.service: search` plus `service-route: frontend`, and its container declares only containerPort 8082 (gRPC) and 9092 (named metrics) — it has no listener on the frontend Service's port 5000.

Exactly two pods in the cluster carry label `service-route=frontend`: frontend-5566ddfbfb-f9vj8 (10.244.7.217, owner ReplicaSet frontend-5566ddfbfb) and search-9cd459687-5ghvg (10.244.125.41, owner ReplicaSet search-9cd459687).

Both the `frontend` and `search` Deployments are at generation 2 and were last written by manager `OpenAPI-Generator` at 2026-11-24T01:17:45Z and 2026-11-24T01:17:46Z, creating ReplicaSets frontend-5566ddfbfb and search-9cd459687; the `rate` Deployment stayed at generation 1, written only at creation (01:17:31Z).

The pre-change ReplicaSet templates frontend-68745cb99c and search-567bb6c4b8 carried only label `io.kompose.service` (plus pod-template-hash) and no `service-route` label, so the `service-route: frontend` label on the current pods was introduced by the 01:17:45/01:17:46 Deployment updates.

The blackbox probe on the frontend Service (`probe_success{instance="frontend.hotel-reservation:5000"}`) returned 0 at 01:18:04Z with `probe_duration_seconds` 5.0004 s, whereas at 01:17:04Z the same probe returned 0 with a 0.0046 s duration, and `probe_success{instance="search.hotel-reservation:8082"}` returned 1 at 01:18:04Z.

The frontend pod frontend-5566ddfbfb-f9vj8 was serving successfully in the newest sampled traces (01:18:03.75–01:18:03.99Z): HTTP GET /hotels returned http.status_code=200 nine times and HTTP GET /recommendations once, with all 141 shown spans carrying no error status; its logs contain only startup lines and its container has 0 restarts.

The search service itself was healthy in the same newest trace sample: `/search.Search/Nearby` server spans ran 1.16–1.88 ms with no error status and its client spans `/rate.Rate/GetRates` ran 0.54–1.14 ms, i.e. search was answering gRPC normally on its own port.

Between 01:17:46.20Z and 01:17:46.55Z the then-current search pod logged repeated `services/search/server.go:252 > downstream request failed dependency=rate grpc_code=Unavailable` (then `Canceled`) warnings and its client spans to rate were marked error; the rate pod only logged `Successfully registered in consul` at 01:17:46.605Z, after those failures.

The rate service's own metrics at 01:18:04Z show RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT 500, rate_queue_capacity 256, rate_requests_received_total 49, rate_requests_completed_total 49, rate_requests_rejected_total 0, rate_requests_expired_total 0, rate_queue_depth 0 and rate_in_flight 0, i.e. its admission limiter was not dropping or expiring requests.
All 19 pods in hotel-reservation were Running and Ready with 0 restarts at the time of query, and no NetworkPolicy objects existed in the namespace (0 items returned in the whole-namespace list).

Cluster events for the namespace show the rollout ordering: frontend Deployment scaled up ReplicaSet frontend-5566ddfbfb at 01:17:45Z and scaled frontend-68745cb99c to 0 at 01:17:46Z, search Deployment scaled up ReplicaSet search-9cd459687 at 01:17:46Z and scaled search-567bb6c4b8 to 0 at 01:17:47Z; no FailedScheduling/Unhealthy/Evicted/OOM events occurred for the frontend or search pods (the only Warning events were FailedScheduling on the deleted pre-change mongodb-geo-78487c9767-hvnwp and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf-s9bt9 pods during PVC binding).

Because the `frontend` Service load-balances port 5000 over both the frontend pod and the search pod, roughly half of the connections arriving at the frontend Service (frontend.hotel-reservation:5000) are steered to a pod with no listener on 5000 and therefore fail instead of reaching the frontend HTTP handler; the 5.0004 s probe failure at 01:18:04, at a moment when the frontend pod was answering /hotels in 3–6 ms, is consistent with this, but whether the failure surfaced as an immediate TCP refusal or a hang is not resolved by the evidence.

Rejected: the rate service (QPS limiter, queue, availability) as the cause of the observed failures. Its counters show 49 received / 49 completed with 0 rejected and 0 expired at 01:18:04Z, its server spans and the search client's rate spans carry no error in the newest sample (0.54–1.14 ms), and the earlier `grpc_code=Unavailable` burst ended before rate finished its Consul registration at 01:17:46.605Z.

Rejected: the search RATE_RPC_* retry settings (RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=1000, RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2, RATE_RPC_INITIAL_BACKOFF_MS=100, RATE_RPC_BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER=2.0, RATE_RPC_JITTER=0.2) as the fault. They do produce two rate client spans per search request, but in the newest sample both attempts succeed (0.54–1.14 ms, no error) and search's own probes/spans are healthy, so no failure is attributable to them.

Restore the `frontend` Service to a selector that matches only frontend pods (its pre-change selector is not visible, but every sibling Service in the namespace uses `io.kompose.service`), or remove the `service-route: frontend` label from the `search` Deployment's pod template, then confirm that the `frontend` Endpoints object lists only frontend pod IPs on port 5000.

Identify the actor behind the `OpenAPI-Generator` writes at 01:17:45Z/01:17:46Z and the `kubectl-patch` write at 01:17:47Z that changed the frontend and search pod-template labels and the frontend Service selector, and confirm no further such changes are pending.

gaps: The pre-change selector value of the `frontend` Service is unknown: metadata.managedFieldsSummary shows a `kubectl-patch` update at 01:17:47Z but not the earlier selector value, and no change-history integration is available (change_history not_integrated).

The exact client-visible error mode is unresolved: the frontend Service probe failed with a 5.0004 s duration rather than an immediate refusal, and no client-side (load generator / ingress) error counts are observable — there is no load-generator pod in the cluster, no Ingress objects exist cluster-wide, and no nginx/ingress metrics are present, so the share of requests lost to the search endpoint is unverified.

No baseline exists from before the change: Prometheus series for this target contain samples only from 01:17:04Z onward (up{job="hotel-reservation-application"} first sample 01:17:04Z) and Jaeger traces were only available for 01:17:46.2–01:18:03.99Z, so no pre/post error-rate or latency comparison is possible.

The span-metrics series traces_span_metrics_calls_total (used by the HighRequestErrorRate/HighRequestLatency rules) returned no data for the namespace, so error-rate and P95 latency alert signals are unknown rather than zero; the alert rules themselves evaluated with no firing alerts.

Container CPU throttling and container CPU/memory usage could not be checked for hotel-reservation: container_cpu_cfs_periods_total, container_cpu_usage_seconds_total and kube_endpoint_address queries for namespace hotel-reservation returned no data, so resource-exhaustion as an alternative cause is unchecked rather than excluded.

Search pods' errors at 01:17:46 (downstream rate Unavailable) were attributed to rate's cold start from timing and rate counters, but the search pod of that moment (search-567bb6c4b8-46m44) no longer exists and its full log stream beyond the returned lines was not read.
Whether the same `service-route: frontend` label pattern exists in other application namespaces cannot be compared: no other application namespace with such Services is present in this cluster.
next_steps: Revert the `frontend` Service selector to its original workload label (or drop `service-route: frontend` from the `search` Deployment) and re-check that `kubectl get endpoints frontend -n hotel-reservation` lists only frontend pod IPs on port 5000.
Add a readiness/selector check (or a NetworkPolicy-free admission check) that fails when a Service's endpoints include pods that do not expose the Service's targetPort.
Capture a request-failure count at the client/ingress layer (e.g., nginx or load-generator metrics) so the fraction of port-5000 connections landing on the search pod can be quantified.
Attribute the `OpenAPI-Generator` and `kubectl-patch` writes of 01:17:45–01:17:47Z in the change-audit system before closing the incident.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

notes: Container hotel-reserv-frontend has no previous instance (HTTP 400: previous terminated container "hotel-reserv-frontend" in pod "frontend-5566ddfbfb-f9vj8" not found); the other streams are unaffected.

view.cannot_prove: A line that is not returned is unknown, not proof that nothing was logged: only limit lines are shown (the newest), and retention, ingest delay, the label selector and line filters can leave gaps. The timestamp is when the line was ingested or parsed, not necessarily when the event happened. A metric query counts only lines inside the query window.

query.jq_expr: .items[] | select(.metadata.name=="frontend" or .metadata.name=="search") | {kind: .kind, name: .metadata.name, created: .metadata.creationTimestamp, labels: .metadata.labels, mf: .metadata.managedFieldsSummary, selector: .spec.selector, tmplLabels: .spec.template.metadata.labels}

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

view.span_groups_note: span_groups summarizes the spans shown in content; spans the adapter sampled out are not counted in any group.
